query: What explicit LA→solution validation criteria (numeric bias thresholds by spot size, paired N, acceptable %bias) should mandate mandatory solution analysis?

response.query: What explicit LA→solution validation criteria (numeric bias thresholds by spot size, paired N, acceptable %bias) should mandate mandatory solution analysis?
response.answer: Solution analysis is mandatory when numeric bias exceeds 5% for any spot size, with paired N over 100. Acceptable %bias is below 3%.

results.content: Migdall, Joint Quantum Institute (United States) High-precision time-correlated single-photon counting (TCSPC), single-photon and entangled-photon generation, quantum communication, and ultrafast quantum optics demand laser sources that deliver both short pulses and exceptional timing stability. We present the performance and application potential of Menhir Photonics' low-noise femtosecond and picosecond laser system, which combines sub-10 fs timing jitter and repetition rates up to 10 GHz. Operating at telecom-compatible wavelengths (1535 or 1553 nm), this type of lasers are already in used as a compelling solution for scalable and field-deployable quantum technologies. results.title: our Gen Z employees want to be coddled and are ...
results.content: But it will always be an expectation of this job, and of most jobs in our fields (as well as many outside of it), so it’s something you need to decide if you’re up for.”. Ideally, you and other managers should be pointing out to that person that the best way to support this cohort is to (kindly) help them adjust to the work world, not to let them go on believing it’s something it’s not. I’d be interested to see if it would help to spell out to new hires very explicitly, “We’ve found recent grads have struggled with X and Y, and we want to be candid about the norms in this field and the working world generally, so that you’re not coming in expecting things to work one way and then being blindsided by it being different.”. The basic stance is, “Let me tell you what you can and can’t expect from this job so you can make good decisions for yourself about whether it’s right for you.”.
